y1: Very early on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to look at the tomb. With a great earthquake, an angel rolled back the stone and sat on it. The Roman guards became like dead men from fear.
y2: The angel's declaration: “He is not here, for He has risen, just as He said.” The stone was rolled away not for Jesus to come out, but for us to “come and see.” The empty tomb was opened as evidence.
y3: At that time, the testimony of women was not accepted in court. If they had made up the resurrection story, they would not have made women the first witnesses. This is a clue showing that the record is true. The women who stayed by the cross to the end heard the first news of the resurrection.
y5: The women ran “with fear and great joy.” At that moment, Jesus met them, saying “Greetings” (chairete, “rejoice”). The women held Jesus' feet and worshiped Him. He had risen bodily, not as a ghost.
y6: Jesus calls the disciples “My brothers.” Even those disciples who had all fled. According to the promise in 26:32, He tells them to meet in Galilee. The resurrection is a declaration of forgiveness and restoration for the failed disciples.
y7: In 12:49–50, Jesus said that whoever does the will of the Father is “My brother.” For the first time after His resurrection, He calls the disciples brothers. Through the cross and resurrection, we became God's family.
y8: The truth they tried to cover with money
y9: Hearing the guards' report, the chief priests and elders consulted together and gave the soldiers “a large sum of money”: “Say that His disciples came by night and stole Him away while we were sleeping.”
y10: How can a sleeping person know who stole something? The lie was contradictory from the start. But they also admitted one thing: the tomb was empty. The conspiracy that started with thirty pieces of silver tried to cover the truth with money again, but failed.
y11: The empty tomb (admitted even by enemies), the testimony of the women, more than 500 witnesses (1 Cor. 15:6), the dramatic change and martyrdom of the disciples who had fled, and the birth of the church. It is hard to explain all of this without the resurrection.
y13: The eleven disciples saw Jesus on the mountain in Galilee and worshiped Him. “But some doubted.” Jesus gives the mission to everyone, without leaving out those who doubted.
y14: “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me. Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.”
y15: There is one main command: “make disciples.” “Go,” “baptize,” and “teach” are the ways to do it. The “teaching” that began in the Sermon on the Mount now goes to all nations. Through the cross and resurrection, Jesus received the “authority of all the kingdoms of the world” that Satan offered to give Him in 4:8.
verse: “Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.”
prayer: Risen Jesus, thank You for the grace of conquering death and raising up the failed disciples again by calling them brothers. Trusting in the Lord who has all authority in heaven and on earth, let me live as a person who goes and makes disciples wherever I am. Immanuel, who is always with us to the end of the age, I glorify You. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: angel. The “angel of the Lord” who appeared to Joseph in chapters 1–2 appears again at the end. “His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing white as snow” (28:3).
d1: worship. The wise men in chapter 2, the disciples in the boat in chapter 14, the women and disciples in chapter 28. From beginning to end, Matthew portrays Jesus as God who is worthy of worship. 4:10 “You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him only shall you serve.”
d2: authority. After the authority of teaching in 7:29 and the authority to forgive sins in 9:6, now it is “all” authority in heaven and on earth. This is the fulfillment of the authority given to the Son of Man in Daniel 7:14. Therefore, we who “go” are not afraid.
